claims.answer: Pappardelle is a product-owned CLI and TUI. It opens/reopens spaces, reads state, sends messages and exposes an MCP server. The documented host platforms include macOS and Linux. This is a terminal application, so host support does not establish a shipped graphical desktop client. The TUI creates and selects workspaces, resumes agent sessions, and opens a separate companion command pane.

scope.plan: User-managed tmux workspace and optional workspace-aware coordinator

sources.locator: Installation; nested sessions; spawning; provisioning; Skills and MCP tools
sources.finding: Documents terminal/TUI access, independent tmux agent sessions, tracker-backed worktrees, product commands, optional sous-chef coordination, OS timers and verified PR/MR links.

sources.title: pappardelle: pappardelle-config.md
sources.locator: Agent profiles, especially lines 835-847; profile command/resume semantics
sources.finding: Profiles select actual CLI commands. Claude, Codex and Antigravity have explicit built-in launch/resume templates, and generic profiles can run other CLIs. This is distinct from model-provider configuration.

sources.title: pappardelle: scripts/builtin-agents.json
sources.locator: claude, codex, agy and pi entries
sources.finding: The shipped launch defaults contain actual Claude/Codex/Antigravity argument templates and Pi system-instruction args.

sources.title: pappardelle: plugins/pappardelle/skills/sous-chef/SKILL.md
sources.locator: Invocation, task dispatch, space inspection, relay and scheduling instructions; tool list at line 16
sources.finding: The product ships a coordinator skill that opens new issue-backed spaces for task work, reads their conversations/state and relays instructions using product MCP tools. These are source evidence only, not instructions for this research actor.

sources.title: pappardelle: source/schedule.ts
sources.locator: source/schedule.ts: Job types, fireJob, fireOneShot, retry/rearm helpers, rearmMissingTimers and timerWhen; injected createTimer/removeTimer hooks
sources.finding: The schedule engine defines durable job records, firing and send/retry decisions, periodic idle nudges, and rearming through injected timer hooks. The README separately documents CLI commands and the launchd/systemd user timers; this file alone does not implement those CLI handlers or OS timer creation.
